Wikipedia: Blake used intaglio engraving for his Illustrations of the Book of Job

highlight.text: Blake employed intaglio engraving in his own work, such as for his Illustrations of the Book of Job, completed just before his death.
they demonstrate that he made frequent use of a technique known as "repoussage", a means of obliterating mistakes by hammering them out by hitting the back of the plate.

work.text: Aged 65, Blake began work on illustrations for the Book of Job, later admired by John Ruskin, who compared Blake favourably to Rembrandt

The set of drawings made for Mr. Linnell varies much in detail from that for Mr. Butts, and is often finer. The engravings were still further altered ; faces in profile in the drawings are given full view in the prints, and so on.

moment.text: [The Book of Job] is of the highest rank in certain characters of imagination and expression ; in the mode of obtaining certain effects of light, it will also be a very useful example to you.

moment.text: Through Linnell he met Samuel Palmer, who belonged to a group of artists who called themselves the Shoreham Ancients. The group shared Blake's rejection of modern trends and his belief in a spiritual and artistic New Age.

matters.text: With no remaining patrons for his design, few to employ him as an engraver, Blake, in age, was on the verge of want. … From Mr. Linnell alone they drew a commission. He engaged Blake to execute and engrave a duplicate set.
